Why, for an oil filler cap
The standard oil-service compound and the cheapest sensible choice for engine oil, gear oil and hydraulic fluid.
Where the oil runs hotter than NBR can take. Costs far less than FKM and is the step most suppliers never offer
Hot oil and aggressive fluids, at 2–3× the cost of NBR. Specify it against a measured temperature
Moderate oil resistance with better weathering, for a filler that is exposed as well as oily
Wide temperature range, but it swells in hot mineral oil and tears easily on a cap pulled off by hand
the pair that fixes a leak
The cap and the seal come as a pair
A leaking filler is usually two worn parts, not one — the cap that has hardened and the O-ring under it that has set. We supply both, and quoting them together is one job rather than two.
Weather compounds do not belong in oil

A filler cap sits in hot oil vapour for the life of the machine. NBR is the standard answer, AEM above +120 °C. Compounds chosen for sunlight and ozone swell and soften in oil — we will say so rather than quote one.
Sized to the bore, not to a catalogue
The cap seals on interference against the filler neck, so the bore diameter is the specification — send that and the depth, and the removal force you can accept, and the rest follows.
Sealed and vented are different parts
Some fillers must breathe through the cap and some must not. Fit the wrong one and the pressure leaves through another seal, which is a leak nobody traces back to a cap. Tell us which you need.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Cap and seal ordered as a set count as two part numbers. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — and measure the neck, not the cap. A cap that has been in oil in the wrong compound has swollen, so it measures larger than it was moulded and copying it gives a part that will not go on. The bore is the only dimension that has not changed.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?
PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. For this part the bore diameter and depth are usually enough — add the oil temperature at the neck, whether it must vent, and how much force is acceptable to open it by hand.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, and the sealing lip is gauged against the neck bore on every batch.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Caps and seals ship bagged and labelled by part number.
